subject: python
title: Variables & Data Types
description: How Python names values, and what the four everyday built-in types do.

content.title: Definition
content.body: A variable is a name bound to a value. Python has no declaration keyword and no type annotation requirement — assigning to a name creates it, and the name can later be rebound to a value of a different type.

content.title: The four you use daily
content.body: int, float, str and bool cover almost all beginner code. type() tells you what you are holding.
content.code:
count = 3          # int
ratio = 0.75       # float
name = "Anna"      # str
active = True      # bool

print(type(ratio))  # <class 'float'>

content.title: Watch out
content.body: Reading a name before anything was assigned to it raises NameError, not a silent None. And "3" is a str, not an int — input() always hands you text.
content.code:
age = input("Age: ")
print(age + 1)     # TypeError
print(int(age) + 1)  # works

exercises.question: What happens when you assign a string to a name that already holds an int?

answers.text: Nothing — the first assignment fixes the type for good
The name is rebound to the string; the int is simply forgotten
The string is converted to an int

exercises.explanation: Names in Python are labels, not typed boxes. Rebinding a name is always allowed, and the old value is collected once nothing refers to it.

exercises.question: What does this print?
exercises.explanation: / is true division and always returns a float. // is floor division and returns an int when both operands are ints.

exercises.question: A Python variable name may start with a digit, for example 2nd_place.
exercises.explanation: Identifiers must start with a letter or underscore. 2nd_place is a SyntaxError; second_place is fine.

exercises.question: input() returns text. Complete the line so the comparison works on numbers.
exercises.explanation: int() parses the text into an integer. Comparing a str with an int raises TypeError in Python 3.

exercises.question: Which line raises the error?

answers.text: Line 1 — total must be declared with a type
Line 3 — price cannot be assigned after use
Line 2 — price is used before it is assigned

exercises.explanation: Python executes top to bottom, so at line 2 the name price does not exist yet and NameError is raised.

exercises.question: Which expression builds the text "Anna is 30" from name = "Anna" and age = 30?
exercises.explanation: An f-string interpolates the expressions in braces. Without the f prefix the braces stay literal, and concatenating a str with an int raises TypeError.

exercises.question: Complete the sentence.
exercises.sentence: An empty string is ___ in a boolean context.
exercises.explanation: Empty containers and zero values are falsy: "", 0, 0.0, [], {} and None all fail an if test.

exercises.back: Swaps two names in one statement — the right side is built as a tuple first
exercises.explanation: Python evaluates the whole right-hand side before binding, so no temporary variable is needed.

exercises.question: What is printed?
exercises.explanation: True division always produces a float, even when the result has no fractional part: 4 / 2 is 2.0.
